2. In a small bowl, mix the shelled sunflower seeds with low sodium soy sauce until they are evenly coated.
3. Add dried oregano and dried basil to the sunflower seeds, and stir well to ensure the herbs are evenly distributed.
4. Spread the seasoned sunflower seeds in a single layer on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
5. Roast in the preheated oven for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally to prevent burning, until the seeds are golden brown and crispy.
6. Remove from the oven and let them cool completely before serving or storing in an airtight container.

Name: Chicken Bone Broth
Preparation:
1. Gather all ingredients: 150.0 g chicken bones, 5.0 ml apple cider vinegar, 30.0 g of carrot, celery, and onion (combined weight), 1.0 tsp paprika, and 1.0 tsp garlic powder.
2. Place the chicken bones in a large pot and cover them with water (approximately 2-3 liters, depending on pot size).
3. Add 5.0 ml of apple cider vinegar to the pot to help extract nutrients from the bones.
4. Roughly chop the carrot, celery, and onion (totaling 30.0 g) and add them to the pot for flavor.
5. Add 1.0 tsp of paprika and 1.0 tsp of garlic powder to enhance the broth's taste.
6. Bring the mixture to a boil over medium-high heat, then reduce to a low simmer.
7. Skim off any foam or impurities that rise to the surface during the initial boiling.
8. Cover the pot partially with a lid and let it simmer for 12-24 hours, occasionally checking and adding more water if needed to keep the bones submerged.
9. After simmering, strain the broth through a fine mesh strainer or cheesecloth into a clean container, discarding the solids.
10. Allow the broth to cool to room temperature, then refrigerate. Skim off any fat that solidifies on the surface before use.
11. Use the chicken bone broth as a base for soups, stews, or sauces, or enjoy it on its own as a warm beverage.

Name: Egg White Omelette with Bell Peppers
Preparation:
1. Separate the egg whites from the yolks of 4 large eggs and place the egg whites in a bowl. Discard the yolks or save them for another recipe.
2. Whisk the egg whites until they are slightly frothy.
3. Dice the red and yellow bell peppers into small pieces, totaling 50 grams.
4. Heat a non-stick frying pan or skillet over medium heat and add 5 grams of olive oil, ensuring it coats the bottom of the pan evenly.
5. Add the diced bell peppers to the pan and sauté for 2-3 minutes, or until they start to soften.
6. Pour the whisked egg whites over the bell peppers in the pan, spreading them out evenly.
7. Cook the omelette for 3-5 minutes, or until the egg whites are set and no longer runny. You can gently lift the edges with a spatula to check if it’s cooked underneath.
8. Once cooked, carefully fold the omelette in half or roll it up, if desired.
9. Slide the omelette onto a plate and serve immediately.

Name: Aloe Vera and Lemon Juice
Preparation:
1. Extract 30.0 g of fresh edible Aloe Vera gel from the Aloe Vera leaf by cutting it open and scooping out the clear gel with a spoon. Ensure to avoid the yellow latex part as it can be bitter and harmful.
2. In a blender or mixing bowl, combine the Aloe Vera gel with 10.0 ml of freshly squeezed lemon juice.
3. Add 150.0 ml of water to the mixture to dilute it and blend or stir until it forms a smooth consistency.
4. If desired, add 5.0 g of honey to sweeten the drink. Stir well to ensure the honey is fully dissolved.
5. Sprinkle 1.0 tsp of dried basil and 1.0 tsp of dried oregano into the mixture for added flavor. Stir gently to mix the herbs evenly.
6. Pour the prepared juice into a glass and serve chilled or at room temperature, as per preference. Optionally, you can strain the mixture before serving if you prefer a smoother texture.
7. Enjoy the refreshing and healthy Aloe Vera and Lemon Juice!

Name: Baked Sweet Potato Fries
Preparation:
1. Preheat your oven to 425°F (220°C).
2. Wash and peel the sweet potato (if desired), then cut it into evenly sized wedges or fries.
3. In a large bowl, toss the sweet potato wedges with olive oil until they are well coated.
4. Sprinkle smoked paprika and sea salt over the wedges, and toss again to ensure even distribution of the seasoning.
5. Arrange the sweet potato wedges in a single layer on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper or a silicone mat, ensuring they do not overlap.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 25-30 minutes, flipping the fries halfway through to ensure even cooking and crispiness.
7. Remove from the oven once the fries are golden brown and tender.
8. Let them cool slightly before serving. Enjoy as a side dish or snack!

Name: Strawberry and Spinach Smoothie
Preparation:
1. Gather all ingredients: 100g strawberries (frozen or fresh), 50g spinach leaves, 150ml almond milk, 5g chia seeds, 1 tsp dried oregano, and 1 tsp dried basil.
2. Rinse the strawberries (if fresh) and spinach leaves under cold water to remove any dirt or debris.
3. Place the strawberries and spinach leaves into a blender.
4. Pour 150ml of almond milk into the blender.
5. Add 5g of chia seeds to the mixture.
6. Sprinkle in 1 tsp of dried oregano and 1 tsp of dried basil for added flavor.
7. Blend all the ingredients on high speed for 1-2 minutes or until the mixture is smooth and well combined.
8. Check the consistency; if the smoothie is too thick, add a little more almond milk and blend again.
9. Pour the smoothie into a glass and serve immediately for the best taste and texture.

Name: Mixed Berries with Almonds
Preparation:
1. Rinse the mixed berries (strawberries, blueberries, blackberries) thoroughly under cold water and pat them dry with a clean kitchen towel.
2. Place the rinsed berries in a medium-sized bowl.
3. Add the soaked almonds (drained of water) to the bowl with the berries.
4. Sprinkle garlic powder and dried oregano over the mixture.
5. Gently toss all the ingredients together to ensure the berries and almonds are evenly coated with the seasonings.
6. Serve immediately as a healthy snack or store in the refrigerator for a short period if not consuming right away.

Name: Kiwi and Apple Salad
Preparation:
1. Start by peeling the kiwi and dicing it into small, bite-sized pieces. Place the diced kiwi in a medium-sized mixing bowl.
2. Dice the green apple into similar-sized pieces as the kiwi and add them to the same bowl.
3. Sprinkle the chia seeds over the diced fruits in the bowl.
4. Add the paprika and black pepper to the mixture for a hint of spice and flavor.
5. Gently toss all the ingredients together to ensure the spices and chia seeds are evenly distributed.
6. Let the salad sit for 5-10 minutes to allow the flavors to meld together.
7. Serve the kiwi and apple salad chilled as a refreshing side dish.

Name: Pomegranate and Beetroot Juice
Preparation:
1. Gather all ingredients: 100g pomegranate seeds, 50g peeled beetroot, 5g mint leaves, 1 tsp dried basil, and 1 tsp garlic powder.
2. Rinse the pomegranate seeds and mint leaves under cold water to remove any dirt or impurities.
3. Cut the peeled beetroot into small chunks for easier blending.
4. Add the pomegranate seeds, beetroot chunks, and mint leaves into a blender or juicer.
5. Sprinkle in the dried basil and garlic powder for added flavor.
6. Blend all the ingredients together until you achieve a smooth consistency. If the mixture is too thick, add a little water to adjust the texture.
7. Strain the juice through a fine mesh sieve or cheesecloth to remove any pulp or seeds, if desired.
8. Pour the juice into a glass and serve immediately for maximum freshness. Optionally, chill in the refrigerator for 15-20 minutes before serving.
9. Garnish with a sprig of mint or a slice of beetroot on the rim of the glass for presentation.

Name: Egg and Mushroom Bhurji
Preparation:
1. Crack the 2 large eggs into a bowl, whisk them well, and set aside.
2. Heat a non-stick pan or skillet over medium heat and add 5.0 g of butter or ghee. Allow it to melt and coat the pan evenly.
3. Add 30.0 g of finely chopped onion and green chili to the pan. Sauté for 2-3 minutes until the onions turn translucent and slightly golden.
4. Add 80.0 g of diced button mushrooms to the pan. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the mushrooms release their water and become tender.
5. Sprinkle 1.0 tsp of dried oregano and 1.0 tsp of garlic powder over the mushroom mixture. Stir well to combine the flavors.
6. Pour the whisked eggs into the pan with the mushroom mixture. Stir continuously to scramble the eggs and mix them evenly with the vegetables.
7. Cook for 2-3 minutes or until the eggs are fully cooked and fluffy, stirring occasionally to avoid sticking to the pan.
8. Turn off the heat and transfer the Egg and Mushroom Bhurji to a serving plate.
9. Serve hot as a main course with bread, roti, or paratha, or enjoy it as a snack on its own.

Name: Sliced Mango with Chia Seeds
Preparation:
1. Peel and cube the ripe mango into bite-sized pieces, measuring approximately 150.0 g, and place them in a serving bowl.
2. Hydrate the chia seeds by soaking 10.0 g of chia seeds in water for about 10-15 minutes until they form a gel-like consistency, then drain any excess water if necessary.
3. Sprinkle the hydrated chia seeds evenly over the cubed mango.
4. Add 1.0 tsp of paprika over the mango and chia seed mixture for a subtle smoky flavor.
5. Finally, sprinkle 1.0 tsp of dried basil on top to enhance the aroma and taste.
6. Gently toss the ingredients together to ensure even distribution of the spices.
7. Serve immediately as a refreshing and nutritious snack.

Name: Oats and Almond Milk Porridge
Preparation:
1. In a small saucepan, combine the rolled oats and unsweetened almond milk.
2. Place the saucepan over medium heat and bring the mixture to a gentle simmer, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking.
3. Cook for about 5-7 minutes or until the oats are soft and have absorbed most of the almond milk, stirring frequently to achieve a creamy consistency.
4. Once the porridge reaches your desired consistency, reduce the heat to low and stir in the cinnamon powder, black pepper, and dried oregano to add flavor.
5. Remove the saucepan from the heat and transfer the porridge to a serving bowl.
6. Drizzle honey on top if desired for a touch of sweetness.
7. Serve the oats and almond milk porridge warm and enjoy!

Name: Avocado and Cacao Mousse
Preparation:
1. Scoop out the flesh of the ripe avocado (60.0 g) into a blender or food processor.
2. Add the raw cacao powder (10.0 g) and honey (10.0 g) to the blender.
3. Include the dried oregano (1.0 tsp) and garlic powder (1.0 tsp) for a unique savory twist to the mousse.
4. Blend all the ingredients together until smooth and creamy, ensuring there are no lumps. If needed, scrape down the sides of the blender to incorporate everything evenly.
5. Taste and adjust sweetness or seasoning if desired by adding a bit more honey or a pinch more of oregano/garlic powder.
6. Transfer the mousse into a serving bowl or individual dessert cups.
7. Chill in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes to allow the flavors to meld and the mousse to set slightly.
8. Serve cold, optionally garnished with a sprinkle of cacao powder or a drizzle of honey on top.

Name: Cucumber and Tomato Salad
Preparation:
1. Wash the cucumber and tomato thoroughly under running water.
2. Dice the cucumber and tomato into small, bite-sized pieces.
3. In a mixing bowl, combine the diced cucumber and tomato.
4. Drizzle 5.0 g of olive oil over the vegetables.
5. Add 5.0 g of lemon juice and a pinch of salt to taste.
6. Toss the salad gently to ensure the ingredients are well mixed and coated with the dressing.
7. Serve immediately as a fresh side dish.

Name: Walnuts and Raisins
Preparation:
1. Measure out 20.0 g of walnuts and 15.0 g of raisins (kishmish) into a small mixing bowl.
2. Add 1.0 tsp of black pepper and 1.0 tsp of paprika to the bowl.
3. Mix all the ingredients thoroughly to ensure the walnuts and raisins are evenly coated with the spices.
4. Serve immediately as a healthy snack or store in an airtight container for later consumption.

Name: Green Tea and Lemon
Preparation:
1. Boil 200 ml of water in a kettle or saucepan until it reaches a rolling boil.
2. Place 2.0 g of green tea leaves (or 1 green tea bag) in a cup or teapot.
3. Pour the boiling water over the green tea leaves or tea bag.
4. Let the tea steep for 2-3 minutes to extract the flavor and nutrients.
5. Strain the tea leaves (if using loose leaves) or remove the tea bag from the cup.
6. Add 5.0 ml of lemon juice to the brewed green tea and stir well.
7. Sprinkle 1.0 tsp of dried oregano and 1.0 tsp of black pepper into the tea.
8. Stir the mixture thoroughly to combine all the flavors.
9. Serve the green tea and lemon hot, and enjoy as a refreshing beverage.

Name: Greek Yogurt with Sunflower Seeds
Preparation:
1. Take 100.0 g of plain Greek yogurt in a small bowl.
2. Add 15.0 g of raw sunflower seeds to the yogurt.
3. Drizzle 5.0 g of honey over the mixture, if desired, for a touch of sweetness.
4. Sprinkle 1.0 tsp of dried basil evenly on top.
5. Add 1.0 tsp of black pepper for a hint of spice.
6. Mix all the ingredients together until well combined.
7. Serve immediately and enjoy as a healthy snack.

Name: Carrot and Ginger Soup
Preparation:
1. Heat the olive oil in a medium-sized pot over medium heat.
2. Add the chopped carrots and grated ginger to the pot. Sauté for about 5 minutes until they start to soften.
3. Stir in the garlic powder and dried basil, and cook for another 1-2 minutes until fragrant.
4. Pour in the vegetable broth and bring the mixture to a boil.
5. Reduce the heat to low, cover the pot, and let it simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until the carrots are very tender.
6. Use an immersion blender or transfer the soup to a blender to puree until smooth. If using a blender, be cautious with the hot liquid and blend in batches if necessary.
7. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed. If the soup is too thick, add a little more vegetable broth or water to reach desired consistency.
8. Serve hot, garnished with a sprinkle of dried basil or a drizzle of olive oil if desired.

Name: Papaya and Pumpkin Seed Salad
Preparation:
1. Start by peeling and cubing 150.0 g of ripe papaya into bite-sized pieces and place them in a mixing bowl.
2. Add 15.0 g of roasted pumpkin seeds to the bowl with the papaya cubes for a crunchy texture.
3. Drizzle 5.0 ml of lime juice over the papaya and pumpkin seeds to add a tangy flavor.
4. Sprinkle 1.0 tsp of paprika and 1.0 tsp of black pepper over the mixture for a hint of spice and seasoning.
5. Gently toss all the ingredients together to ensure they are evenly coated with the lime juice and spices.
6. Let the salad sit for 5 minutes to allow the flavors to meld together.
7. Serve the papaya and pumpkin seed salad chilled or at room temperature as a refreshing side dish.

Name: Tomato and Celery Juice
Preparation:
1. Wash the tomatoes and celery stalks thoroughly under running water to remove any dirt or impurities.
2. Cut the tomatoes into small chunks for easier blending.
3. Trim the ends of the celery stalks and chop them into smaller pieces.
4. Add the chopped tomatoes and celery to a blender or juicer.
5. Blend the mixture until it becomes a smooth juice. If using a blender, you may need to strain the juice through a fine mesh sieve to remove pulp, depending on your preference.
6. Pour the juice into a glass.
7. Sprinkle black pepper on top of the juice for added flavor.
8. Stir gently to mix the pepper into the juice.
9. Serve immediately and enjoy your refreshing tomato and celery juice.

Name: Coconut Water and Lime
Preparation:
1. Pour 250 ml of fresh coconut water into a glass or a pitcher.
2. Add 10 ml of freshly squeezed lime juice to the coconut water and stir well to combine.
3. Sprinkle 1 teaspoon of paprika into the mixture and mix thoroughly to ensure it is evenly distributed.
4. Add 1 teaspoon of dried basil to the drink and stir gently to incorporate the flavors.
5. Optionally, chill the beverage in the refrigerator for 10-15 minutes or serve over ice for a refreshing experience.
6. Serve immediately and enjoy the unique blend of coconut water, lime, and spices.

Name: Strawberry and Almond Smoothie
Preparation:
1. Wash the strawberries thoroughly under running water to remove any dirt or impurities.
2. In a blender, add the washed strawberries, soaked and peeled almonds, and almond milk.
3. Blend the ingredients on high speed until you achieve a smooth consistency.
4. Add garlic powder and dried basil to the blender.
5. Blend again for a few seconds to mix the spices evenly into the smoothie.
6. Pour the smoothie into a glass and serve immediately for the best taste and freshness.

Name: Boiled Egg Whites with Spinach
Preparation:
1. Boil the Eggs: Place 4 large eggs in a saucepan and cover them with water. Bring the water to a boil over medium-high heat. Once boiling, reduce the heat to low and let the eggs simmer for 10-12 minutes. After cooking, transfer the eggs to a bowl of ice water to cool. Once cooled, peel the eggs and carefully separate the egg whites from the yolks. Set the egg whites aside.
2. Prepare the Spinach: Rinse 100 grams of spinach thoroughly under running water to remove any dirt or impurities. Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat. Add the spinach leaves with a splash of water and sauté for 2-3 minutes until the spinach wilts and becomes tender. Stir occasionally to ensure even cooking. Remove from heat and set aside.
3. Combine Ingredients: Chop the boiled egg whites into bite-sized pieces. In a mixing bowl, combine the chopped egg whites and sautéed spinach.
4. Season the Dish: Sprinkle 5 grams of black pepper and lemon juice over the egg white and spinach mixture. Toss gently to ensure the seasoning is evenly distributed.
5. Serve: Transfer the mixture to a serving plate. Serve immediately as a healthy side dish or snack.

Name: Almonds and Pumpkin Seeds
Preparation:
1. Soak the almonds in water for 6-8 hours or overnight. After soaking, peel the skin off the almonds and pat them dry with a clean towel.
2. In a mixing bowl, combine the peeled almonds and raw pumpkin seeds.
3. Add the dried basil and dried oregano to the bowl with the almonds and pumpkin seeds.
4. Toss everything together to ensure the nuts and seeds are evenly coated with the herbs.
5. Optionally, you can lightly toast the mixture in a dry pan over low heat for 2-3 minutes to enhance the flavors, stirring continuously to avoid burning.
6. Let the mixture cool if toasted, then transfer to an airtight container for storage or serve immediately as a healthy snack.

Name: Citrus Salad (Orange and Grapefruit)
Preparation:
1. Start by peeling the orange and grapefruit, then carefully segment them by cutting between the membranes to release the individual segments. Place the segments in a mixing bowl.
2. Finely chop the mint leaves and add them to the bowl with the citrus segments.
3. Sprinkle the black pepper and dried oregano over the mixture.
4. Gently toss all the ingredients together to ensure the citrus segments are evenly coated with the herbs and spices.
5. Let the salad sit for 5-10 minutes to allow the flavors to meld.
6. Serve the citrus salad chilled or at room temperature as a refreshing side dish.

Name: Cucumber and Pineapple Juice
Preparation:
1. Wash and peel the cucumber, then cut it into small pieces.
2. Prepare the pineapple by ensuring it is cut into chunks if not already done.
3. Rinse the mint leaves thoroughly under running water.
4. Add the cucumber pieces, pineapple chunks, and mint leaves into a blender.
5. Blend the ingredients until smooth.
6. Strain the juice through a fine mesh sieve into a glass or jug to remove any pulp, if desired.
7. Add black pepper and dried basil to the juice and stir well to combine.
8. Serve the cucumber and pineapple juice chilled by adding ice cubes or refrigerating it for a while before serving.

Name: Oats and Egg White Omelet
Preparation:
1. In a blender or food processor, grind the rolled oats into a fine powder and set aside.
2. Finely chop the onion and green chili.
3. In a mixing bowl, whisk the egg whites until they are slightly frothy.
4. Add the powdered rolled oats, chopped onion, green chili, dried basil, and garlic powder to the egg whites. Mix well to combine all ingredients evenly.
5. Heat a non-stick frying pan or skillet over medium heat and add the olive oil, ensuring it coats the pan evenly.
6. Pour the egg white and oats mixture into the pan, spreading it out to form an even layer.
7. Cook for 3-4 minutes on one side or until the edges start to lift and the bottom is golden brown.
8. Carefully flip the omelet using a spatula and cook the other side for another 2-3 minutes until fully cooked.
9. Once done, transfer the omelet to a plate and serve hot.

Name: Roasted Red Bell Pepper Soup
Preparation:
1. Preheat your oven to 200°C (400°F). Place the red bell peppers (150.0 g) on a baking sheet and roast them for about 25-30 minutes, turning occasionally, until the skins are charred and blistered.
2. Remove the peppers from the oven and place them in a bowl. Cover with plastic wrap or a lid and let them steam for 10 minutes. This will make it easier to peel off the skins.
3. Peel the skins off the roasted red bell peppers, remove the seeds and stems, and roughly chop the flesh.
4. In a pot, heat olive oil (5.0 g) over medium heat. Add the roasted garlic (10.0 g) and sauté for 1-2 minutes until fragrant.
5. Add the chopped roasted red bell peppers to the pot and stir for another 2-3 minutes.
6. Pour in the vegetable broth (200.0 ml) and bring the mixture to a boil. Reduce the heat to low and let it simmer for 15-20 minutes to allow the flavors to meld.
7. Use an immersion blender or transfer the soup to a blender to puree until smooth. If using a blender, be cautious with the hot liquid and blend in batches if necessary.
8. Return the soup to the pot (if blended separately) and heat through. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper if needed.
9. Serve hot, optionally garnished with a drizzle of olive oil or a sprinkle of fresh herbs.

Name: Almonds and Dried Figs (Anjeer)
Preparation:
1. Soak the almonds in water for 6-8 hours or overnight. After soaking, peel the skin off the almonds and set them aside.
2. Rinse the dried figs (anjeer) under running water to remove any dirt or impurities, then pat them dry with a clean cloth or paper towel.
3. In a small bowl, mix the black pepper and paprika together to create a spice blend.
4. Take a serving plate or bowl and arrange the peeled almonds and dried figs together.
5. Sprinkle the black pepper and paprika mixture evenly over the almonds and figs.
6. Toss gently to ensure the spices coat the almonds and figs lightly.
7. Serve immediately as a healthy and flavorful snack.

Name: Quinoa and Lentil Salad
Preparation:
1. Cook the quinoa according to package instructions, then let it cool to room temperature. Ensure you have 60.0 g of cooked quinoa ready.
2. Boil the brown lentils until tender but not mushy, then drain and cool. Measure out 60.0 g of boiled lentils.
3. Dice the cucumber and tomato into small, bite-sized pieces, totaling 50.0 g.
4. In a large mixing bowl, combine the cooled quinoa, boiled lentils, and diced cucumber and tomato.
5. In a small bowl, mix 10.0 g of lemon juice and olive oil to create a dressing.
6. Pour the dressing over the quinoa and lentil mixture, tossing gently to coat evenly.
7. Sprinkle 1.0 tsp of paprika and 1.0 tsp of dried basil over the salad.
8. Mix everything together until the spices are well distributed.
9. Serve the salad chilled or at room temperature as a refreshing side dish.

Name: Carrot and Apple Salad
Preparation:
1. In a large mixing bowl, combine the grated carrots and chopped green apple.
2. Drizzle the lemon juice over the carrot and apple mixture to prevent browning and add a tangy flavor.
3. Sprinkle garlic powder and paprika over the mixture for added seasoning.
4. Toss all the ingredients together until they are evenly mixed and coated with the spices and lemon juice.
5. Let the salad sit for 5-10 minutes to allow the flavors to meld.
6. Serve chilled or at room temperature as a refreshing side dish.

Name: Peanut Butter and Banana on Whole Wheat
Preparation:
1. Toast the whole wheat bread slice lightly if desired, or use it as is.
2. Spread 20 g of natural peanut butter evenly over one side of the bread slice.
3. Peel and slice the banana (50 g) into thin rounds.
4. Arrange the banana slices neatly over the peanut butter.
5. Sprinkle 1 tsp of paprika and 1 tsp of black pepper evenly over the banana slices for added flavor.
6. Serve immediately and enjoy as a quick, nutritious snack.

Name: Watermelon and Mint Cooler
Preparation:
1. Cut the deseeded watermelon (200 g) into small cubes and place them in a blender.
2. Add fresh mint leaves (5 g) to the blender with the watermelon.
3. Pour in lime juice (5 ml) for a tangy flavor.
4. Sprinkle black pepper (1 tsp) and garlic powder (1 tsp) into the mixture for a unique savory twist.
5. Blend all the ingredients together until smooth.
6. Strain the mixture through a fine mesh sieve to remove any pulp, if desired, for a smoother texture.
7. Pour the cooler into a glass over ice cubes.
8. Garnish with a sprig of mint or a slice of lime, if desired.
9. Serve chilled and enjoy your refreshing Watermelon and Mint Cooler.

Name: Kiwi and Chia Seed Bowl
Preparation:
1. Start by preparing the chia seeds. In a small bowl, mix 15.0 g of chia seeds with about 60 ml of water. Let it sit for 10-15 minutes or until the seeds have absorbed the water and formed a gel-like consistency.
2. While the chia seeds are hydrating, peel and dice 150.0 g of kiwi into small, bite-sized pieces.
3. In a serving bowl, combine the diced kiwi and the hydrated chia seeds. Mix gently to ensure an even distribution.
4. Drizzle 5.0 g of honey over the mixture if desired for added sweetness. Stir lightly to incorporate the honey.
5. Sprinkle 1.0 tsp of dried oregano and 1.0 tsp of black pepper over the top for a unique flavor twist.
6. Serve immediately as a refreshing and nutritious snack.

Name: Celery and Apple Juice
Preparation:
1. Wash the celery stalks and green apple thoroughly under running water to remove any dirt or impurities.
2. Cut the celery stalks into smaller pieces to fit into a juicer or blender.
3. Core the green apple and cut it into chunks.
4. Add the celery and apple pieces into a juicer or blender. If using a blender, add a small amount of water to help with blending.
5. Process the mixture until it becomes a smooth juice. If using a blender, strain the mixture through a fine mesh sieve or cheesecloth to separate the juice from the pulp.
6. Pour the extracted juice into a glass.
7. Add the lemon juice, garlic powder, and dried oregano to the juice.
8. Stir well to combine all the ingredients.
9. Serve the celery and apple juice immediately, preferably chilled, for the best flavor and nutritional benefits.

Name: Boiled Green Peas
Preparation:
1. If using fresh green peas, shell them from the pods. If using frozen peas, they can be used directly.
2. Bring a pot of water to a boil. Add a pinch of salt to the water.
3. Add the green peas to the boiling water and cook for 3-5 minutes or until they are tender but still vibrant green. Avoid overcooking to maintain their texture and color.
4. Drain the peas using a colander and rinse them briefly under cold water to stop the cooking process.
5. In a pan, melt the butter or ghee over low heat.
6. Add the boiled green peas to the pan and toss them gently to coat with the butter or ghee.
7. Sprinkle black pepper and salt over the peas and mix well to ensure even seasoning.
8. Serve hot as a side dish.

Name: Papaya and Yogurt Bowl
Preparation:
1. Take a bowl and add 100 grams of plain yogurt (dahi) as the base.
2. Cube 100 grams of ripe papaya and layer it over the yogurt.
3. Sprinkle 5 grams of ground flaxseeds evenly on top for added texture and nutrition.
4. Add 1 teaspoon of dried basil to enhance the flavor profile with a subtle herbal note.
5. Finally, sprinkle 1 teaspoon of black pepper for a hint of spice.
6. Mix gently if desired, or enjoy the layers as is. Serve immediately for a refreshing and healthy snack.

Name: Carrot and Tomato Soup
Preparation:
1. Heat olive oil in a pot over medium heat.
2. Add chopped garlic and black pepper, sauté for 1-2 minutes until fragrant.
3. Add chopped carrots and tomatoes to the pot, stirring well to coat them with the oil and spices.
4. Pour in enough water or vegetable broth (about 2-3 cups) to cover the vegetables.
5. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and let it simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the carrots are tender.
6. Use an immersion blender or transfer the mixture to a blender to puree the soup until smooth.
7. Return the soup to the pot (if blended separately), adjust seasoning if needed, and heat through.
8. Serve hot, garnished with a drizzle of olive oil or fresh herbs if desired.

Name: Pomegranate and Mint Salad
Preparation:
1. Start by deseeding the pomegranate and collect 150.0 g of fresh pomegranate seeds in a mixing bowl.
2. Rinse 10.0 g of fresh mint leaves under running water to remove any dirt or impurities, then pat them dry with a clean kitchen towel. Roughly chop or tear the mint leaves and add them to the bowl with the pomegranate seeds.
3. In a small bowl, mix 5.0 g of lime juice and black salt until well combined.
4. Drizzle the lime juice and black salt mixture over the pomegranate seeds and mint leaves.
5. Gently toss everything together to ensure the ingredients are evenly coated with the dressing.
6. Let the salad sit for 5-10 minutes to allow the flavors to meld together.
7. Serve the pomegranate and mint salad chilled as a refreshing side dish.

Name: Roasted Soybeans
Preparation:
1. Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C).
2. Rinse the dry soybeans under cold water to remove any dust or debris, then pat them dry with a clean towel.
3. Spread the soybeans in a single layer on a baking sheet.
4. Roast the soybeans in the preheated oven for about 30-40 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they are golden brown and crispy.
5. Remove the soybeans from the oven and let them cool slightly.
6. In a small bowl, mix the sea salt and paprika together.
7. Sprinkle the sea salt and paprika mixture over the roasted soybeans and toss to coat evenly.
8. Allow the soybeans to cool completely before serving or storing in an airtight container.

Name: Tomato and Ginger Juice
Preparation:
1. Wash the tomatoes thoroughly under running water to remove any dirt or impurities.
2. Peel the fresh ginger using a peeler or a spoon to remove the skin.
3. Cut the tomatoes into small chunks for easier blending.
4. Grate or finely chop the ginger to extract maximum flavor.
5. Add the tomato chunks and ginger into a blender or juicer.
6. Blend the mixture until it becomes a smooth puree or juice.
7. Strain the juice through a fine mesh sieve or cheesecloth to remove any pulp or seeds, if desired.
8. Add black pepper to the juice and stir well to combine.
9. Pour the tomato and ginger juice into a glass.
10. Serve immediately, optionally with ice cubes for a refreshing drink.

Name: Almonds and Walnuts
Preparation:
1. Soak the almonds and walnuts in water for 6-8 hours or overnight to soften them. 
2. After soaking, peel the skin off the almonds for a smoother texture. 
3. Drain the water from both almonds and walnuts and pat them dry with a clean kitchen towel. 
4. In a small bowl, mix the dried oregano and garlic powder. 
5. Toss the soaked and peeled almonds and walnuts with the oregano and garlic powder mixture until they are evenly coated. 
6. Optionally, you can roast the seasoned nuts in a preheated oven at 350°F (175°C) for 10-12 minutes for a crispy texture, stirring halfway to ensure even roasting. 
7. Let the nuts cool completely before serving. 
8. Store in an airtight container for up to a week to maintain freshness.

Name: Orange and Strawberry Bowl
Preparation:
1. Start by peeling the orange and carefully segmenting it into bite-sized pieces, removing any seeds or excess pith. Place the orange segments into a medium-sized mixing bowl.
2. Wash the strawberries thoroughly under cold water, pat them dry with a paper towel, and cut them in half. Add the halved strawberries to the bowl with the orange segments.
3. Rinse the mint leaves under cold water and pat them dry. Finely chop the mint leaves and sprinkle them over the fruit mixture for a refreshing flavor.
4. Add the dried oregano and garlic powder to the bowl. These spices will provide a unique savory contrast to the sweetness of the fruits.
5. Gently toss all the ingredients together to ensure the spices and mint are evenly distributed over the fruit.
6. Let the bowl sit for 5-10 minutes to allow the flavors to meld together.
7. Serve the Orange and Strawberry Bowl fresh as a healthy snack, either chilled or at room temperature, based on your preference.

Name: Carrot and Celery Soup
Preparation:
1. Heat the olive oil in a medium-sized pot over medium heat.
2. Add the chopped carrots and celery to the pot and sauté for about 5-7 minutes, or until they start to soften.
3. Stir in the paprika and dried oregano, and cook for another 1-2 minutes to release their aromas.
4. Pour in the vegetable broth and bring the mixture to a boil.
5. Reduce the heat to low, cover the pot, and let it simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until the vegetables are tender.
6. Use an immersion blender to puree the soup until smooth, or transfer to a blender in batches and blend until creamy.
7. Taste and adjust seasoning if necessary, then serve hot.

Name: Papaya and Lime Salad
Preparation:
1. Peel the ripe papaya (150.0 g) and remove the seeds. Cut the papaya into small, bite-sized cubes or thin slices as per your preference.
2. Place the papaya pieces in a mixing bowl.
3. Drizzle 10.0 ml of lime juice over the papaya pieces to add a tangy flavor.
4. Sprinkle 1.0 g of black salt evenly over the salad for a unique, savory taste.
5. Gently toss the ingredients together to ensure the lime juice and black salt are well distributed.
6. Let the salad sit for 5-10 minutes to allow the flavors to meld.
7. Serve the papaya and lime salad chilled or at room temperature as a refreshing side dish.

Name: Orange and Carrot Juice
Preparation:
1. Wash and peel the oranges, then cut them into smaller pieces for easier blending or juicing.
2. Wash and peel the carrots, then chop them into small chunks.
3. Peel the ginger and grate or finely chop it.
4. Add the oranges, carrots, and ginger into a blender or juicer.
5. Blend or juice the ingredients until smooth. If using a blender, you may need to strain the mixture through a fine mesh sieve or cheesecloth to remove pulp, depending on your preference.
6. Stir in the paprika and garlic powder to the juice for added flavor.
7. Pour the juice into a glass and serve immediately, preferably chilled or over ice.

Name: Coconut Water with Chia Seeds
Preparation:
1. Pour 250.0 ml of fresh coconut water into a glass or a jar.
2. Add 10.0 g of chia seeds to the coconut water and stir well to ensure the seeds are evenly distributed.
3. Let the mixture sit for about 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, to allow the chia seeds to absorb the liquid and form a gel-like consistency.
4. Add 5.0 ml of lime juice to the mixture and stir to combine.
5. Sprinkle 1.0 tsp of garlic powder and 1.0 tsp of black pepper into the drink, and mix thoroughly to incorporate the flavors.
6. Serve chilled or at room temperature, stirring once more before drinking to ensure an even distribution of ingredients.

Name: Kiwi and Strawberry Salad
Preparation:
1. Start by washing the kiwi and strawberries thoroughly under running water to remove any dirt or impurities.
2. Peel the kiwi and dice it into small, bite-sized pieces. Place the diced kiwi in a medium-sized mixing bowl.
3. Cut the strawberries in half and add them to the bowl with the kiwi.
4. Finely chop the fresh mint leaves and sprinkle them over the fruit mixture for a refreshing flavor.
5. Add the dried basil and dried oregano to the bowl, ensuring they are evenly distributed over the fruits.
6. Gently toss all the ingredients together to combine the flavors, being careful not to mash the fruits.
7. Let the salad sit for 5-10 minutes to allow the flavors to meld.
8. Serve the kiwi and strawberry salad chilled as a refreshing side dish.

Name: Egg White and Spinach Wrap
Preparation:
1. Prepare the Ingredients: Separate the egg whites from 4 large eggs into a bowl. Rinse and roughly chop 30 g of fresh spinach. Measure out 5 g of olive oil, 1 tsp of dried oregano, and 1 tsp of dried basil.
2. Cook the Egg Whites: Heat a non-stick skillet or frying pan over medium heat and add the olive oil. Once the oil is warm, pour in the egg whites. Stir gently to ensure even cooking. Add the chopped spinach, dried oregano, and dried basil. Continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until the egg whites are fully set and the spinach is wilted, about 3-5 minutes.
3. Warm the Tortilla: While the egg mixture is cooking, warm the whole wheat tortilla or roti on another pan or directly over a low flame for about 10-15 seconds on each side until it is soft and pliable.
4. Assemble the Wrap: Place the warmed tortilla on a flat surface. Spoon the cooked egg white and spinach mixture onto the center of the tortilla. Fold the bottom of the tortilla up over the filling, then fold in the sides and roll tightly to close.
5. Serve: Cut the wrap in half if desired and serve immediately while warm.

Name: Tomato and Cucumber Salad
Preparation:
1. Wash and dice 150.0 g of tomatoes and 150.0 g of cucumber into bite-sized pieces.
2. Place the diced tomatoes and cucumber into a mixing bowl.
3. Drizzle 10.0 g of olive oil and lemon juice over the vegetables.
4. Finely chop 5.0 g of mint leaves and sprinkle them over the salad.
5. Add 1.0 tsp of black pepper and 1.0 tsp of dried basil to the mixture.
6. Toss all the ingredients together gently to ensure they are evenly coated with the dressing and spices.
7. Let the salad sit for 5-10 minutes to allow the flavors to meld.
8. Serve fresh as a side dish.

Name: Apple and Beetroot Juice
Preparation:
1. Wash and peel the beetroot and green apple thoroughly.
2. Cut the beetroot and green apple into small chunks for easier blending.
3. Add the beetroot and green apple chunks into a blender or juicer.
4. Blend or juice the ingredients until smooth.
5. Strain the juice through a fine mesh sieve or cheesecloth to remove any pulp, if desired.
6. Pour the juice into a glass.
7. Add lemon juice, paprika, and garlic powder to the juice.
8. Stir well to combine all the flavors.
9. Serve immediately, preferably chilled, or over ice for a refreshing drink.

Name: Spinach and Cucumber Smoothie
Preparation:
1. Wash the fresh spinach (100.0 g) thoroughly under running water to remove any dirt or impurities.
2. Peel and chop the cucumber (150.0 g) into small pieces for easier blending.
3. In a blender, add the washed spinach, chopped cucumber, lemon juice (10.0 ml), dried basil (1.0 tsp), and garlic powder (1.0 tsp).
4. Blend all the ingredients on high speed until you achieve a smooth consistency. If the mixture is too thick, you can add a little water to adjust the texture.
5. Once blended, pour the smoothie into a glass.
6. Serve immediately to enjoy the fresh flavors, or refrigerate for a short time if you prefer it chilled.

Name: Pineapple and Mint Salad
Preparation:
1. Start by peeling and cutting the pineapple into small, bite-sized cubes. Measure out 150.0 g of the cubed pineapple and place it in a mixing bowl.
2. Rinse the fresh mint leaves under cold water to remove any dirt or impurities. Pat them dry with a clean kitchen towel, then roughly chop or tear the leaves (5.0 g) to release their aroma.
3. Add the chopped mint leaves to the bowl with the pineapple cubes.
4. Sprinkle 1.0 g of black salt over the pineapple and mint mixture for a tangy flavor.
5. Gently toss all the ingredients together to ensure the black salt and mint are evenly distributed.
6. Transfer the salad to a serving dish or individual bowls.
7. Serve immediately for the freshest taste, or chill in the refrigerator for 10-15 minutes if you prefer a cooler salad.

Name: Hard Boiled Eggs with Black Pepper
Preparation:
1. Place the 2 large eggs in a saucepan and cover them with cold water.
2. Bring the water to a boil over medium-high heat.
3. Once the water reaches a rolling boil, turn off the heat and cover the saucepan with a lid.
4. Let the eggs sit in the hot water for 10-12 minutes for hard-boiled eggs.
5. After the time is up, carefully transfer the eggs to a bowl of ice water to stop the cooking process and cool them down for about 5 minutes.
6. Peel the eggs by gently tapping them on a hard surface to crack the shell, then remove the shell under running water if needed.
7. Slice the eggs in half or keep them whole, as per preference.
8. Sprinkle 1.0 g of black pepper evenly over the eggs for flavor.
9. Serve immediately as a snack or store in the refrigerator for later consumption.

Name: Almond and Cashew Mix
Preparation:
1. Soak the almonds in water for 6-8 hours or overnight. After soaking, peel the skin off the almonds and pat them dry with a clean cloth or paper towel.
2. In a mixing bowl, combine the peeled almonds and cashews.
3. Add dried oregano and garlic powder to the nut mix. Toss well to ensure the nuts are evenly coated with the seasonings.
4. Preheat a non-stick pan or skillet over medium heat. Add the seasoned nut mix to the pan.
5. Roast the nuts for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally to prevent burning, until they turn slightly golden and aromatic.
6. Remove from heat and let the almond and cashew mix cool completely.
7. Store in an airtight container and enjoy as a healthy snack.

Name: Quinoa and Green Peas
Preparation:
1. Rinse 60.0 g of quinoa thoroughly under running water to remove any bitterness.
2. Cook the quinoa in a pot with water (use a ratio of 1:2, quinoa to water) over medium heat for about 15 minutes or until it absorbs all the water and becomes fluffy. Set aside.
3. In a separate pot, boil 50.0 g of green peas in water for 5-7 minutes or until tender. Drain and set aside.
4. Heat a pan over medium heat and add 5.0 g of ghee, allowing it to melt.
5. Add the cooked quinoa and boiled green peas to the pan. Mix well to coat them evenly with ghee.
6. Sprinkle 1.0 g of black pepper over the mixture and stir for 1-2 minutes to combine the flavors.
7. Turn off the heat and serve hot as a main course or side dish.

Name: Papaya and Cucumber Cooler
Preparation:
1. Peel and deseed the papaya (100 g), then cut it into small chunks.
2. Peel the cucumber (150 g) and chop it into small pieces.
3. In a blender, add the papaya chunks, cucumber pieces, and mint leaves (5 g).
4. Add garlic powder (1 tsp) and paprika (1 tsp) to the blender for a unique flavor twist.
5. Blend all the ingredients until smooth. If needed, add a little water to achieve the desired consistency.
6. Strain the mixture through a fine mesh sieve to remove any pulp, if a smoother texture is preferred.
7. Pour the cooler into a glass, garnish with a mint leaf if desired, and serve chilled.

Name: Orange and Spinach Juice
Preparation:
1. Peel the orange and cut it into smaller pieces for easier blending.
2. Wash the fresh spinach thoroughly to remove any dirt or impurities.
3. Peel the ginger and grate it finely.
4. In a blender, add the orange pieces, spinach, and grated ginger.
5. Blend the ingredients on high speed until you achieve a smooth consistency.
6. Add black pepper and paprika to the mixture and blend for an additional 10-15 seconds to mix the spices evenly.
7. If the juice is too thick, add a little water to reach your desired consistency and blend again.
8. Strain the juice through a fine mesh sieve or cheesecloth if you prefer a smoother texture without pulp.
9. Pour the juice into a glass and serve immediately for the freshest taste.

Name: Egg White and Avocado Toast
Preparation:
1. Toast the whole wheat bread in a toaster or on a skillet until it is golden brown and crispy.
2. In a non-stick skillet, heat 2.0 g of olive oil over medium heat.
3. Pour the 3.0 large egg whites into the skillet and cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they are fully cooked and scrambled. Season with a pinch of salt if desired.
4. Spread 30.0 g of mashed avocado evenly over the toasted whole wheat bread.
5. Top the avocado toast with the cooked egg whites.
6. Sprinkle 1.0 tsp of paprika and 1.0 tsp of garlic powder evenly over the egg whites for added flavor.
7. Serve immediately and enjoy your Egg White and Avocado Toast!

Name: Carrot and Beetroot Salad
Preparation:
1. Wash and peel the carrots and beetroot. Grate them finely using a grater and place them in a mixing bowl.
2. Add lemon juice to the grated carrots and beetroot for a tangy flavor.
3. Sprinkle black pepper and dried basil over the mixture for seasoning.
4. Toss all the ingredients together until well combined.
5. Let the salad rest for 5-10 minutes to allow the flavors to meld.
6. Serve chilled or at room temperature as a refreshing side dish.

Name: Oat and Almond Milk Porridge
Preparation:
1. In a small saucepan, combine 50.0 g of rolled oats and 200.0 ml of unsweetened almond milk.
2. Place the saucepan over medium heat and bring the mixture to a gentle simmer, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking.
3. Reduce the heat to low and cook for 5-7 minutes, or until the oats are soft and have absorbed most of the almond milk, stirring frequently for a creamy consistency.
4. Stir in 5.0 g of ground flaxseeds, 1.0 tsp of dried basil, and 1.0 tsp of dried oregano, mixing well to evenly distribute the flavors.
5. Cook for an additional 1-2 minutes on low heat, allowing the flavors to meld.
6. Remove from heat and let the porridge sit for a minute before transferring it to a serving bowl.
7. Serve warm, optionally topped with additional toppings like nuts, seeds, or fresh herbs if desired.

Name: Orange and Grapefruit Bowl
Preparation:
1. Start by peeling the orange and grapefruit. Carefully segment them by removing the pith and membrane, ensuring only the juicy flesh remains. Place the segments in a medium-sized mixing bowl.
2. Finely chop the fresh mint leaves and sprinkle them over the citrus segments for a refreshing aroma and flavor.
3. Add the dried basil and black pepper to the bowl, evenly distributing the seasonings over the fruit.
4. Gently toss all the ingredients together to ensure the flavors are well combined without breaking the fruit segments.
5. Let the mixture sit for 5-10 minutes to allow the flavors to meld together.
6. Serve the orange and grapefruit bowl chilled as a refreshing side dish.

Name: Cucumber and Lemon Water
Preparation:
1. Wash the cucumber and lemon thoroughly under running water to remove any dirt or impurities.
2. Slice the cucumber (with skin) into thin rounds, approximately 100 grams.
3. Slice the lemon into thin rounds, approximately 50 grams.
4. In a large pitcher or jar, add 500 ml of clean, cold water.
5. Add the sliced cucumber and lemon to the water.
6. Sprinkle 1 teaspoon of dried basil and 1 teaspoon of dried oregano into the mixture.
7. Stir gently to combine all the ingredients.
8. Let the mixture infuse for at least 1-2 hours in the refrigerator to allow the flavors to meld.
9. Serve chilled, optionally with ice cubes, and enjoy as a refreshing beverage.

Name: Hard Boiled Egg Whites with Turmeric
Preparation:
1. Place 4 large eggs in a saucepan and cover them with water. Bring the water to a boil over medium-high heat. Once boiling, reduce the heat to low and let the eggs simmer for 10-12 minutes. 
2. After boiling, carefully transfer the eggs to a bowl of ice water to cool for about 5 minutes. This will make peeling easier. 
3. Peel the eggs and discard the yolks, keeping only the egg whites. 
4. Cut the egg whites into halves or quarters, depending on your preference. 
5. In a small bowl, mix 2.0 g of turmeric powder and 1.0 g of black pepper. 
6. Sprinkle the turmeric and black pepper mixture evenly over the egg whites. 
7. Serve immediately as a healthy snack or store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days.

Name: Papaya and Pomegranate Bowl
Preparation:
1. Start by peeling the papaya and removing the seeds. Cut the papaya into small, bite-sized cubes and place them in a mixing bowl.
2. Add the pomegranate seeds to the bowl with the cubed papaya.
3. Finely chop the mint leaves and sprinkle them over the fruit mixture for a fresh flavor.
4. Season the bowl with paprika and garlic powder, ensuring the spices are evenly distributed by gently tossing the ingredients together.
5. Serve the papaya and pomegranate bowl immediately as a refreshing snack, or chill it in the refrigerator for 10-15 minutes for a cooler taste.

Name: Soaked Black Raisins
Preparation:
1. Take 20.0 g of black raisins (Kala Kishmish) in a small bowl.
2. Add water to the bowl, enough to completely submerge the raisins, and let them soak for 6-8 hours or overnight until they become plump and soft.
3. After soaking, drain the excess water from the raisins using a strainer.
4. Transfer the soaked raisins to a mixing bowl.
5. Add 1.0 tsp of garlic powder and 1.0 tsp of dried basil to the raisins.
6. Mix well to ensure the raisins are evenly coated with the garlic powder and dried basil.
7. Let the mixture sit for 10-15 minutes to allow the flavors to meld.
8. Serve as a healthy and flavorful snack.

Name: Sweet Potato and Spinach Hash
Preparation:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
2. Add the cubed sweet potato to the skillet and cook for about 10-12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sweet potato is tender and slightly golden.
3. Sprinkle the paprika over the sweet potato and stir to coat evenly.
4. Add the fresh spinach to the skillet and cook for an additional 2-3 minutes, stirring frequently, until the spinach is wilted.
5. Remove from heat and serve warm as a side dish.

Name: Kiwi and Cucumber Cooler
Preparation:
1. Wash and peel the kiwi (100 g) and cucumber (100 g).
2. Cut the kiwi and cucumber into small chunks for easier blending.
3. In a blender, add the kiwi chunks, cucumber chunks, and mint leaves (5 g).
4. Blend the ingredients until smooth. If needed, add a small amount of water to achieve the desired consistency.
5. Strain the mixture through a fine mesh sieve to remove any pulp, if a smoother texture is preferred.
6. Stir in the dried basil (1 tsp) and paprika (1 tsp) to add a subtle flavor kick.
7. Pour the cooler into a glass, garnish with a mint leaf if desired, and serve chilled.

Name: Quinoa and Almond Porridge
Preparation:
1. Rinse the quinoa thoroughly under cold water to remove any bitterness.
2. In a medium saucepan, combine the rinsed quinoa and almond milk. Bring to a boil over medium heat.
3. Once boiling, reduce the heat to low, cover the saucepan, and let it simmer for about 15 minutes or until the quinoa is tender and has absorbed most of the almond milk.
4. Stir in the crushed almonds, garlic powder, and dried oregano. Mix well to ensure the flavors are evenly distributed.
5. Cook for an additional 2-3 minutes on low heat, stirring occasionally.
6. Remove from heat and let it sit for a couple of minutes before serving.
7. Serve warm as a savory porridge, optionally garnished with additional crushed almonds or fresh herbs if desired.

Name: Roasted Bell Pepper Soup
Preparation:
1. Preheat your oven to 200°C (400°F).
2. Wash and dry the red bell peppers (150.0 g). Cut them in half, remove the seeds and stems, and place them cut-side down on a baking tray.
3. Drizzle the bell peppers with olive oil (5.0 g) and roast them in the preheated oven for about 25-30 minutes, or until the skins are charred and blistered.
4. Remove the peppers from the oven and place them in a bowl. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap or a lid and let them steam for 10 minutes to loosen the skins.
5. Peel off the charred skins from the bell peppers and set the flesh aside.
6. In a medium pot, heat a small amount of olive oil over medium heat. Add minced garlic (5.0 g) and sauté for 1-2 minutes until fragrant, being careful not to burn it.
7. Add the roasted bell pepper flesh to the pot and stir to combine with the garlic.
8. Pour in enough vegetable broth or water (about 500 ml) to cover the peppers. Bring to a simmer and cook for 10 minutes to allow the flavors to meld.
9. Use an immersion blender or transfer the mixture to a blender to puree the soup until smooth. If using a blender, be cautious with the hot liquid.
10. Season the soup with salt and pepper to taste. Optionally, add a splash of cream or a dollop of yogurt for a creamier texture.
11. Serve hot, garnished with a drizzle of olive oil or fresh herbs if desired.

Name: Walnut and Fig Mix
Preparation:
1. Soak the walnuts and dried figs in water for 4-6 hours or overnight to soften them.
2. After soaking, drain the water from the walnuts and figs.
3. Roughly chop the soaked figs into small pieces.
4. In a mixing bowl, combine the soaked walnuts and chopped figs.
5. Add black pepper and paprika to the mixture and toss well to coat evenly.
6. Serve immediately as a healthy snack or store in an airtight container for later use.

Name: Spinach and Celery Juice
Preparation:
1. Wash the fresh spinach and celery stalks thoroughly under running water to remove any dirt or impurities.
2. Chop the spinach and celery into smaller pieces for easier blending.
3. Add the chopped spinach and celery into a blender or juicer.
4. Pour in the lemon juice to enhance the flavor and add a tangy note.
5. Sprinkle in the dried basil and paprika for added depth and a hint of spice.
6. Blend all the ingredients together until you achieve a smooth consistency. If using a juicer, process the ingredients to extract the juice.
7. If the mixture is too thick, you can add a small amount of water to reach your desired consistency.
8. Strain the juice through a fine mesh sieve or cheesecloth if you prefer a smoother texture without pulp.
9. Pour the juice into a glass and serve immediately to enjoy the maximum freshness and nutritional benefits.
10. Optionally, you can chill the juice in the refrigerator for a refreshing cold drink.

Name: Toasted Pumpkin and Sunflower Seeds
Preparation:
1. Preheat a non-stick skillet or frying pan over medium heat.
2. Add the hulled pumpkin seeds and sunflower seeds to the skillet.
3. Toast the seeds for about 5-7 minutes, stirring frequently to prevent burning, until they turn golden brown and emit a nutty aroma.
4. Once toasted, reduce the heat to low and sprinkle the dried basil and garlic powder over the seeds.
5. Stir well to evenly coat the seeds with the seasonings.
6. Continue to cook for an additional 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly to ensure the spices are well distributed.
7. Remove the skillet from the heat and let the seeds cool completely.
8. Once cooled, transfer the toasted seeds to an airtight container for storage or serve immediately as a snack.

Name: Papaya and Lemon Bowl
Preparation:
1. Peel and cube the papaya into bite-sized pieces, measuring out 200.0 g.
2. Place the cubed papaya in a serving bowl.
3. Squeeze fresh lemon juice, measuring 10.0 ml, and drizzle it evenly over the papaya.
4. Sprinkle 1.0 g of black salt over the papaya and lemon mixture.
5. Gently toss the ingredients to ensure the lemon juice and black salt are evenly distributed.
6. Serve immediately as a refreshing snack.

Name: Almond and Pistachio Mix
Preparation:
1. Soak the almonds in water for 6-8 hours or overnight to soften them.
2. After soaking, peel the skin off the almonds for a smoother texture.
3. Take 15.0 g of soaked and peeled almonds and 15.0 g of raw, unsalted pistachios.
4. Mix the almonds and pistachios together in a bowl or container.
5. Serve as a healthy snack or store in an airtight container for later use.

Name: Beetroot and Apple Juice
Preparation:
1. Wash and peel the beetroot and green apple thoroughly under running water to remove any dirt or impurities.
2. Cut the beetroot and green apple into small chunks for easier blending or juicing.
3. Peel the ginger and grate it finely to extract maximum flavor.
4. Add the beetroot, green apple, and grated ginger into a blender or juicer. If using a blender, you may need to add a small amount of water (about 50-100 ml) to help with the blending process.
5. Blend or juice the ingredients until you get a smooth consistency.
6. If blended, strain the mixture through a fine mesh sieve or cheesecloth to separate the juice from the pulp. If using a juicer, this step may not be necessary.
7. Pour the juice into a glass or container.
8. Add garlic powder and dried basil to the juice and stir well to combine the flavors.
9. Optionally, chill the juice in the refrigerator for 15-20 minutes before serving for a refreshing taste.
10. Serve the beetroot and apple juice fresh, garnished with a small basil leaf if desired.

Name: Guava and Pomegranate Salad
Preparation:
1. Wash and slice 150.0 g of guava into thin, bite-sized pieces.
2. Extract 50.0 g of pomegranate seeds from a fresh pomegranate.
3. In a mixing bowl, combine the sliced guava and pomegranate seeds.
4. Sprinkle 2.0 g of chaat masala over the mixture for flavor.
5. Add 150.0 ml of water to the bowl to lightly hydrate the salad and enhance the taste.
6. Toss everything gently to ensure the chaat masala is evenly distributed.
7. Let the salad sit for 5-10 minutes to allow the flavors to meld.
8. Serve chilled or at room temperature as a refreshing side dish.

Name: Ash Gourd (Winter Melon) Juice
Preparation:
1. Wash, peel, and remove the seeds from the ash gourd. Cut it into small cubes for easier blending.
2. Place the ash gourd cubes in a blender or juicer and blend until smooth. If needed, add a little water to help with blending.
3. Strain the juice through a fine mesh sieve or cheesecloth to remove any pulp, if a clearer juice is desired.
4. Pour the juice into a glass or container.
5. Add lime juice, black pepper, and dried basil to the ash gourd juice. Stir well to combine all the ingredients.
6. Serve the juice chilled by refrigerating it for 30 minutes or adding a few ice cubes.
7. Enjoy the refreshing ash gourd juice immediately.

Name: Bottle Gourd (Lauki) Soup
Preparation:
1. Heat 5.0 g of ghee in a pan over medium heat.
2. Add 2.0 g of cumin seeds to the hot ghee and let them splutter for a few seconds until aromatic.
3. Add 200.0 g of peeled and diced bottle gourd to the pan and sauté for 2-3 minutes.
4. Pour in 2-3 cups of water (or as needed for desired consistency) and bring it to a boil.
5. Reduce the heat to low, cover the pan, and let the bottle gourd simmer for 10-15 minutes or until it becomes soft and tender.
6. Once cooked, use a blender or immersion blender to puree the mixture until smooth.
7. Strain the soup if a finer texture is desired (optional).
8. Return the soup to the pan, adjust the consistency with additional water if needed, and heat it through.
9. Season with salt and pepper to taste (optional).
10. Serve hot in bowls or cups.

Name: Green Papaya Salad (Som Tum)
Preparation:
1. Peel and shred the green papaya into thin strips using a grater or a shredder, and place it in a large mixing bowl. Ensure the papaya is fresh and firm for the best texture.
2. In a small bowl, squeeze fresh lime juice to measure 10.0 ml and set it aside.
3. Add the lime juice to the shredded green papaya and toss well to coat evenly, allowing the citrus flavor to penetrate the papaya.
4. Sprinkle 10.0 g of crushed peanuts over the papaya mixture for added crunch and nutty flavor.
5. Add 1.0 tsp of dried basil and 1.0 tsp of paprika to the bowl, mixing thoroughly to distribute the spices evenly.
6. Taste and adjust the seasoning if needed, ensuring a balance of tangy, spicy, and savory flavors.
7. Transfer the salad to a serving plate and garnish with a few extra crushed peanuts if desired.
8. Serve immediately as a refreshing side dish, ideally paired with grilled meats or sticky rice.

Name: Aloe Vera and Mint Juice
Preparation:
1. Extract the gel from fresh Aloe Vera leaves and wash it thoroughly to remove any bitterness.
2. In a blender, add the washed Aloe Vera gel (50.0 g), fresh mint leaves (10.0 g), water (200.0 ml), black pepper (1.0 tsp), and garlic powder (1.0 tsp).
3. Blend the mixture on high speed for 1-2 minutes until it becomes smooth and well combined.
4. Strain the juice through a fine mesh sieve or cheesecloth to remove any fibrous residue, if desired.
5. Pour the strained juice into a glass.
6. Serve chilled by adding ice cubes or refrigerating the juice for 15-20 minutes before serving.
7. Optionally, garnish with a fresh mint leaf for presentation.

Name: Pineapple and Turmeric Smoothie
Preparation:
1. Gather all the ingredients: 200 g of cubed pineapple, 2 g of turmeric powder, and 1 g of black pepper.
2. Place the cubed pineapple into a blender.
3. Add the turmeric powder and black pepper to the blender.
4. Blend the mixture on high speed until it reaches a smooth consistency. If needed, add a small amount of water or ice to adjust the thickness.
5. Pour the smoothie into a glass and serve immediately for the best flavor and nutritional benefits.

Name: Steamed Sweet Corn Salad
Preparation:
1. Steam the sweet corn kernels (150.0 g) in a steamer or boil them in water for 5-7 minutes until they are tender. Drain any excess water and let them cool slightly.
2. In a mixing bowl, combine the steamed sweet corn kernels with diced bell peppers (50.0 g).
3. Drizzle lemon juice (5.0 ml) over the mixture and toss everything together to ensure the ingredients are well mixed.
4. Serve the steamed sweet corn salad chilled or at room temperature as a refreshing side dish.

Name: Cabbage and Carrot Slaw
Preparation:
1. In a large mixing bowl, combine the finely shredded green cabbage and shredded carrots.
2. In a small bowl, whisk together the apple cider vinegar, dried oregano, and dried basil to create the dressing.
3. Pour the dressing over the cabbage and carrot mixture.
4. Toss everything together until the vegetables are evenly coated with the dressing.
5. Let the slaw sit for at least 10-15 minutes to allow the flavors to meld.
6. Serve chilled or at room temperature as a side dish.

Name: Strawberry and Almond Milk Shake
Preparation:
1. Wash the fresh strawberries (100.0 g) thoroughly under running water to remove any dirt or impurities.
2. Remove the stems from the strawberries and cut them into halves or quarters for easier blending.
3. In a blender, add the chopped strawberries, almond milk (200.0 ml), chia seeds (5.0 g), dried basil (1.0 tsp), and dried oregano (1.0 tsp).
4. Blend all the ingredients on high speed for 1-2 minutes or until the mixture is smooth and well combined.
5. Check the consistency of the milkshake; if it’s too thick, add a little more almond milk and blend again.
6. Pour the strawberry and almond milkshake into a glass.
7. Optionally, garnish with a fresh strawberry or a sprinkle of chia seeds on top.
8. Serve immediately and enjoy your refreshing beverage!

Name: Sauted Mushrooms with Garlic
Preparation:
1. Clean the button mushrooms by wiping them with a damp paper towel or brushing off any dirt. Slice them into even pieces if not already sliced.
2. Heat a pan over medium heat and add the olive oil, allowing it to warm up.
3. Add the minced garlic to the pan and sauté for about 30 seconds or until fragrant, being careful not to burn it.
4. Add the sliced mushrooms to the pan and stir well to coat them in the garlic and oil mixture.
5. Cook the mushrooms for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they release their moisture and turn golden brown.
6. Sprinkle the dried basil and black pepper over the mushrooms, stirring to combine evenly.
7. Continue to cook for another 1-2 minutes to allow the flavors to meld.
8. Remove from heat and serve hot as a side dish.

Name: Pomegranate and Pear Salad
Preparation:
1. Start by preparing the ingredients: deseed the pomegranate to get 100.0 g of seeds, and cube the pear to measure 150.0 g.
2. Wash and pat dry 5.0 g of fresh mint leaves.
3. In a mixing bowl, combine the pomegranate seeds and cubed pear.
4. Sprinkle 1.0 tsp of black pepper and 1.0 tsp of dried oregano over the fruit mixture.
5. Gently toss the salad to evenly distribute the spices.
6. Garnish with the fresh mint leaves on top.
7. Serve immediately as a refreshing side dish.

Name: Tomato and Coriander Juice
Preparation:
1. Wash the tomatoes and fresh coriander (cilantro) thoroughly under running water to remove any dirt or impurities.
2. Roughly chop the tomatoes into small pieces and place them in a blender.
3. Add the fresh coriander leaves to the blender with the tomatoes.
4. Blend the mixture until it forms a smooth puree. If needed, add a little water to help with blending.
5. Strain the juice through a fine mesh sieve or cheesecloth into a glass or jug to remove any pulp or solids, if a smoother texture is desired.
6. Add black salt to the juice and stir well to combine.
7. Serve the tomato and coriander juice chilled or at room temperature, as per preference. Optionally, garnish with a sprig of coriander.

Name: Carrot and Ginger Smoothie
Preparation:
1. Wash and peel the carrots, then chop them into small pieces for easier blending.
2. Peel the ginger and grate it finely to ensure it blends smoothly.
3. In a blender, add the chopped carrots, grated ginger, fresh orange juice, garlic powder, and dried oregano.
4. Blend all the ingredients on high speed until the mixture is completely smooth. If the smoothie is too thick, add a little more orange juice or water to reach your desired consistency.
5. Taste and adjust the flavors if needed, adding more ginger for spice or orange juice for sweetness.
6. Pour the smoothie into a glass and serve immediately for the freshest taste. Optionally, you can chill it in the refrigerator for 10-15 minutes before serving.

Name: Lemon Water with Chia Seeds
Preparation:
1. In a glass or jar, add 15.0 g of chia seeds.
2. Pour 300.0 ml of water into the glass with the chia seeds and stir well to prevent clumping.
3. Let the mixture sit for about 10-15 minutes, allowing the chia seeds to absorb the water and form a gel-like consistency. Stir occasionally to ensure even absorption.
4. Add 15.0 ml of lemon juice to the chia seed mixture and mix thoroughly.
5. Sprinkle 1.0 tsp of dried oregano and 1.0 tsp of black pepper into the drink.
6. Stir everything together to combine the flavors.
7. Serve the lemon water with chia seeds chilled or at room temperature, as per your preference.

Name: Cucumber and Dill Salad
Preparation:
1. Wash and thinly slice the cucumber (200.0 g) into rounds or half-moons, as preferred, and place them in a mixing bowl.
2. Finely chop the fresh dill (10.0 g) and add it to the bowl with the cucumber slices.
3. Drizzle olive oil (5.0 g) over the cucumber and dill mixture.
4. Sprinkle paprika (1.0 tsp) and dried oregano (1.0 tsp) evenly over the salad.
5. Toss all the ingredients together until the cucumber slices are well coated with the oil and seasonings.
6. Let the salad sit for 5-10 minutes to allow the flavors to meld.
7. Serve chilled or at room temperature as a refreshing side dish.

Name: Walnuts and Brazil Nuts Mix
Preparation:
1. Measure 15.0 g of walnuts and 10.0 g of Brazil nuts into a small mixing bowl.
2. Add 1.0 tsp of paprika and 1.0 tsp of dried oregano to the bowl with the nuts.
3. Toss the mixture gently to ensure the nuts are evenly coated with the spices.
4. Serve immediately as a snack or store in an airtight container for later use.

Name: Sauted Spinach with Lemon
Preparation:
1. Heat a large skillet or pan over medium heat and add the olive oil (5.0 g).
2. Once the oil is hot, add the chopped spinach (150.0 g) to the pan and stir occasionally to ensure even cooking.
3. Sauté the spinach for about 2-3 minutes or until it starts to wilt.
4. Sprinkle garlic powder (1.0 tsp) and black pepper (1.0 tsp) over the spinach, stirring to combine the flavors.
5. Continue to cook for another 1-2 minutes until the spinach is fully wilted but still vibrant green.
6. Remove the pan from heat and drizzle the lemon juice (15.0 ml) over the spinach, stirring to mix well.
7. Transfer the sautéed spinach to a serving dish and serve immediately as a side dish.

Name: Kiwi and Cucumber Smoothie
Preparation:
1. Peel the kiwi and cut it into small chunks.
2. Wash the cucumber thoroughly, peel if desired, and cut it into small pieces.
3. Add the kiwi and cucumber pieces into a blender.
4. Add chia seeds, paprika, and black pepper to the blender.
5. Blend all the ingredients together until smooth. If the consistency is too thick, add a little water and blend again.
6. Pour the smoothie into a glass and serve immediately for the best taste and nutrient retention.

Name: Papaya and Lemon Juice
Preparation:
1. Peel and cube 200.0 g of ripe papaya, ensuring to remove the seeds.
2. In a blender, add the cubed papaya and blend until smooth.
3. Add 15.0 ml of lemon juice to the blended papaya and blend again for a few seconds to mix well.
4. Pour the juice into a glass.
5. Sprinkle 1.0 g of black pepper on top of the juice for a slight kick.
6. Stir gently and serve immediately, preferably chilled.

Name: Beetroot and Mint Salad
Preparation:
1. Wash and peel the raw beetroot, then grate it finely into a mixing bowl using a grater.
2. Finely chop the fresh mint leaves and add them to the bowl with the grated beetroot.
3. Drizzle the lemon juice over the beetroot and mint mixture for a refreshing tang.
4. Sprinkle the black pepper and dried oregano evenly over the salad for added flavor.
5. Toss all the ingredients together until well combined, ensuring the seasonings and lemon juice are evenly distributed.
6. Let the salad sit for 5-10 minutes to allow the flavors to meld together.
7. Serve chilled or at room temperature as a refreshing side dish.

Name: Orange and Pomegranate Bowl
Preparation:
1. Peel the orange and carefully separate it into segments, removing any pith or seeds. Place the segments (150.0 g) in a medium-sized bowl.
2. Add the pomegranate seeds (100.0 g) to the bowl with the orange segments.
3. Sprinkle 1.0 tsp of paprika evenly over the fruit mixture for a subtle smoky flavor.
4. Add 1.0 tsp of dried basil to enhance the aroma and add a hint of herbaceous taste.
5. Gently toss the ingredients together to ensure the spices are evenly distributed.
6. Serve immediately as a refreshing and healthy snack, or chill in the refrigerator for 10-15 minutes for a cooler treat.

Name: Boiled Eggs with Black Pepper
Preparation:
1. Place the 2 large eggs in a small saucepan and cover them with cold water.
2. Bring the water to a boil over medium-high heat.
3. Once the water reaches a rolling boil, reduce the heat to low and let the eggs simmer for 9-12 minutes, depending on how firm you want the yolk.
4. Remove the eggs from the saucepan and place them in a bowl of cold water or ice bath to stop the cooking process and make them easier to peel.
5. Once cooled, carefully peel the eggs and place them on a plate.
6. Sprinkle 1.0 g of black pepper evenly over the boiled eggs.
7. Serve immediately as a snack or side dish.

Name: Cabbage and Apple Juice
Preparation:
1. Wash the green cabbage and green apple thoroughly under running water to remove any dirt or impurities.
2. Chop the green cabbage into smaller pieces for easier blending.
3. Core the green apple and cut it into chunks, leaving the skin on for added nutrients if desired.
4. Add the chopped cabbage, apple chunks, and 150 ml of water into a blender.
5. Blend the mixture on high speed until it becomes a smooth liquid. If the consistency is too thick, add a little more water and blend again.
6. Once blended, strain the juice through a fine mesh sieve or cheesecloth into a glass or jug to remove any pulp, if a smoother texture is preferred.
7. Stir in 1 teaspoon of dried basil and 1 teaspoon of paprika to the juice for added flavor. Mix well to ensure the spices are evenly distributed.
8. Serve the cabbage and apple juice chilled by refrigerating it for 15-20 minutes or adding a few ice cubes.
9. Enjoy the refreshing beverage immediately for the best taste and nutritional benefits.

Name: Quinoa and Roasted Vegetable Bowl
Preparation:
1. Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F).
2. Rinse 100.0 g of quinoa under cold water, then cook it according to package instructions (typically, combine quinoa with 200 ml of water, bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes or until water is absorbed). Set aside.
3. While the quinoa is cooking, chop 50.0 g of mixed color bell peppers and 50.0 g of zucchini into bite-sized pieces.
4. Place the chopped vegetables on a baking tray, drizzle with 10.0 g of olive oil, and toss to coat evenly.
5. Roast the vegetables in the preheated oven for 20-25 minutes, or until they are tender and slightly caramelized, stirring halfway through.
6. Once the quinoa and vegetables are ready, combine them in a large bowl and mix gently to distribute the ingredients evenly.
7. Serve warm as a nutritious main course, optionally garnished with fresh herbs or a squeeze of lemon juice for added flavor.

Name: Grilled Lemon Herb Basa Fish
Preparation:
1. In a small bowl, mix lemon juice, mixed herbs, olive oil, paprika, and dried oregano to create a marinade.
2. Place the Basa fish fillet in a shallow dish or a zip-lock bag and pour the marinade over it, ensuring the fish is well-coated.
3. Let the fish marinate for 15-30 minutes in the refrigerator to absorb the flavors.
4. Preheat a grill or grill pan over medium-high heat.
5. Lightly grease the grill with a small amount of olive oil to prevent sticking.
6. Remove the fish from the marinade, allowing excess marinade to drip off, and place it on the hot grill.
7. Grill the fish for about 3-4 minutes on each side, or until it flakes easily with a fork and has nice grill marks.
8. Remove the fish from the grill and let it rest for a couple of minutes.
9. Serve hot with your choice of sides or garnish with fresh herbs and a lemon wedge.

Name: Chicken and Lentil Stew
Preparation:
1. In a medium-sized pot, heat a small amount of oil over medium heat.
2. Add the diced chicken breast to the pot and cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the chicken is browned and nearly cooked through.
3. Add the diced carrots to the pot and sauté for another 3-4 minutes until they begin to soften.
4. Pour in the chicken broth and bring the mixture to a gentle boil.
5. Stir in the cooked red lentils (Masoor Dal), dried oregano, and dried basil.
6. Reduce the heat to low, cover the pot, and let the stew simmer for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the flavors meld together and the chicken is fully cooked.
7. Taste and adjust seasoning if necessary.
8. Serve hot as a hearty main course.

Name: Avocado and Chickpea Salad Wrap
Preparation:
1. Lay the whole wheat tortilla flat on a clean surface.
2. In a small bowl, mash the avocado (50 g) with a fork until smooth.
3. Spread the mashed avocado evenly over the tortilla.
4. Add the boiled chickpeas (50 g) on top of the avocado layer, spreading them out evenly.
5. Place the spinach leaves (20 g) over the chickpeas.
6. Sprinkle dried oregano (1 tsp) and black pepper (1 tsp) evenly over the ingredients.
7. Carefully roll the tortilla tightly from one end to the other to form a wrap.
8. Slice the wrap into halves or smaller pieces if desired.
9. Serve immediately and enjoy your healthy Avocado and Chickpea Salad Wrap!

Name: Mediterranean Tuna Salad
Preparation:
1. Drain the canned tuna thoroughly and place it in a medium-sized mixing bowl.
2. Wash and halve the cherry tomatoes, then add them to the bowl with the tuna.
3. Wash and dice the cucumber into small bite-sized pieces, and add them to the bowl.
4. Drizzle the olive oil over the mixture in the bowl.
5. Sprinkle the garlic powder and dried basil evenly over the ingredients.
6. Gently toss all the ingredients together until they are well combined and coated with the olive oil and seasonings.
7. Serve immediately as a fresh salad or chill in the refrigerator for 15-20 minutes to let the flavors meld before serving.

Name: Lemon Coriander Soup with Grilled Tofu
Preparation:
1. Prepare the Ingredients: Gather all the ingredients. Ensure the tofu is firm and grilled beforehand. Chop the fresh coriander finely if not already done.
2. Heat the Broth: In a medium-sized pot, pour 200 ml of vegetable broth and bring it to a gentle simmer over medium heat.
3. Season the Broth: Add 1 tsp of garlic powder and 1 tsp of black pepper to the simmering broth. Stir well to combine the flavors.
4. Add Lemon Juice: Squeeze in 15 ml of fresh lemon juice into the broth. Stir and let it simmer for 2-3 minutes to allow the flavors to meld.
5. Add Coriander: Add 15 g of chopped fresh coriander to the broth. Stir and cook for another 1-2 minutes. Reserve a small amount of coriander for garnish if desired.
6. Prepare the Tofu: If the tofu is not already grilled, cut 80 g of firm tofu into small cubes or strips, and grill it on a pan or grill until golden brown on all sides. You can lightly season it with a pinch of salt or pepper while grilling.
7. Assemble the Soup: Place the grilled tofu pieces into serving bowls. Pour the hot lemon coriander broth over the tofu.
8. Garnish and Serve: Garnish with a sprinkle of reserved chopped coriander on top. Serve the Lemon Coriander Soup with Grilled Tofu hot as a refreshing side dish.

Name: Tomato and Basil Zucchini Noodles
Preparation:
1. Spiralize the zucchini into noodle-like strands using a spiralizer and set aside.
2. Halve the cherry tomatoes and roughly chop the fresh basil leaves.
3. In a large non-stick pan or skillet, lightly sauté the zucchini noodles over medium heat for 2-3 minutes until they are slightly softened but still retain some crunch. No oil is needed, but you can add a small splash of water if they stick to the pan.
4. Add the halved cherry tomatoes to the pan with the zucchini noodles and cook for another 1-2 minutes until the tomatoes start to soften.
5. Sprinkle in the paprika and dried oregano, stirring well to coat the zucchini and tomatoes evenly with the spices.
6. Remove the pan from heat and toss in the chopped fresh basil, mixing it through the warm noodles and tomatoes.
7. Transfer the zucchini noodle mixture to a serving plate or bowl.
8. Sprinkle the grated Parmesan cheese over the top as a finishing touch.
9. Serve immediately and enjoy your light and healthy Tomato and Basil Zucchini Noodles!

Name: Greek Lemon Chicken with Cucumber Salad
Preparation:
1. Marinate the Chicken: In a bowl, mix 120.0 g of chicken breast with 5.0 ml of olive oil, 1.0 tsp of black pepper, and 1.0 tsp of paprika. Ensure the chicken is well-coated and let it marinate for at least 15-30 minutes to absorb the flavors.
2. Cook the Chicken: Heat a non-stick skillet or grill pan over medium heat. Place the marinated chicken breast in the pan and cook for about 6-8 minutes on each side, or until fully cooked and golden brown. Ensure the internal temperature reaches 165°F (74°C). Once cooked, set aside to rest for 5 minutes before slicing.
3. Prepare the Cucumber Salad: In a separate bowl, combine 100.0 g of diced cucumber with 20.0 g of crumbled feta cheese. Drizzle with a small amount of olive oil (optional) and toss gently to mix.
